course_name_en: APPLICATIONS OF AUTOMATIC CONTROL Single channel

learning_outcomes.text: The student will acquire a better knowledge of the concepts of Automatic Control through the presentation of detailed examples of controller design in different application areas: robotics, communication networks and routing problems, aerospace.
The student will be able to understand and apply general techniques for the analysis and design of control laws to concrete application examples.

The student will be able to identify and critically evaluate the salient aspects of control system design, from drafting specifications to using mathematical models, from synthesis alternatives to implementation aspects, to simulation and evaluation of results.
The course allows the student to present problems of modeling and control of systems in highly topical and applicative engineering fields.
The course aims to encourage autonomous attitudes of analysis and learning oriented to solving problems in automatic engineering.

Knowledge and understanding of the characteristic aspects of applied automatic control in various interdisciplinary domains, including: robotics, biological systems, aerospace systems, cyber-physical security.
Autonomous design of controllers for specific case studies chosen from the illustrated applications.

syllabus_topics: Illustration of selected applications in the following possible areas: robotics, biological systems, biomedical field, aerospace, sensor networks

assessment_methods.method: Oral exam (evaluation and discussion of projects)

assessment_rules: To pass the exam, a grade not lower than 18/30 is required. The student must demonstrate sufficient familiarity with automatic control applications and be able to autonomously design control algorithms for at least two proposed application scenarios, via two group projects to be submitted. The oral exam will consist of the evaluation of the projects and the discussion of the results obtained. To achieve a score of 30/30 cum laude, the student must demonstrate excellent knowledge of all topics related to the themes of the two presented projects.
bibliography: B. Siciliano, L. Sciavicco, L. Villani and G. Oriolo, "Robotics", Springer
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Informatica e Automatica (L-8)
